children.topic: Art. 81 · Principles of the electoral system
children.note: Every part of how Kenya elects its leaders must respect five principles: political freedom, the gender rule, fair representation of disabled people, equal votes for all adults, and free and fair elections.

manas.q: Name the five principles of the electoral system in Article 81.

children.note: Citizens must be free to use the political rights that Article 38 gives them (forming parties, campaigning, voting, standing).
No elective public body may have more than two-thirds of its members of one gender. Put the other way: each gender should hold at least one third of the seats.

manas.q: What does Article 81(b) say about gender in elective bodies?

children.note: Persons with disabilities are to be fairly represented, and every adult votes, with each vote aiming to count equally.
Five marks of a free and fair election.

manas.q: Give three of the five marks of a free and fair election in Article 81(e).

children.note: Nobody can see how you voted.
No intimidation, undue pressure or corruption.
Run by a body that no side controls (the IEBC).
The process can be seen and checked.
Impartial, neutral, efficient, accurate and accountable.

children.topic: Art. 82 · Election laws Parliament must make
children.note: Parliament must pass laws on boundaries, nominations, continuous voter registration, running elections and referenda, and gradually letting Kenyans abroad register and vote. Those laws must make voting simple and open and must cater for disabled people and others with special needs.

Boundaries drawn by the IEBC; how candidates are nominated; registration that never closes for good; how elections and referenda are run and supervised; step-by-step registration and voting for citizens living abroad.
Simple and transparent, with the special needs of disabled voters and other groups taken into account.

manas.q: What three qualities must voting have under Article 82(2)?

children.note: Elections Act 2011 and the IEBC Act 2011. Check the current versions on new.kenyalaw.org (checked 27 Nov 2026).

children.topic: Art. 83 · Who may register as a voter
children.note: An adult citizen may register unless declared of unsound mind or convicted of an election offence in the last five years. Each voter registers at one centre only, and the arrangements must help, not block, eligible citizens.
Adult (18 or over) citizen; not declared of unsound mind; no election-offence conviction in the past five years.

manas.q: What three conditions qualify a person to register as a voter (Article 83)?

children.note: Registering at two centres is not allowed.
Registration and polling arrangements must make it easier, never harder, for an eligible citizen to vote or stand.
At every election, every candidate and every party must follow the code of conduct that the IEBC sets.
The Electoral Code of Conduct is a schedule to the Elections Act. Check the current text on new.kenyalaw.org (checked 27 Nov 2026).

manas.q: Who prescribes the electoral code of conduct, and who must obey it?

children.note: You may stand without a party if you have not been a party member for at least three months before the election. You also need the voter support that Article 99 (Parliament) or Article 193 (county assembly) requires.
Leave your party at least three months before polling day.

manas.q: How long must an independent candidate have been out of a party before the election?

children.note: Election on 8 August: a would-be independent who resigned from a party on 1 June has a gap of under ten weeks, so does not qualify; resigning on or before 8 May would.
National Assembly: 1,000 registered voters in the constituency; Senate: 2,000 in the county (Article 99(1)(c)).

children.topic: Art. 86 · How voting and counting must be done
children.note: Whatever method is used, the IEBC must make voting simple, accurate, checkable, secure, accountable and open. Votes are counted and announced at each polling station, then collated openly by the returning officer, with safeguards against malpractice.
Six qualities, whether paper or electronic: simple, accurate, verifiable, secure, accountable, transparent.
The presiding officer counts, tabulates and announces the result right there, promptly.

manas.q: Where are votes first counted and announced under Article 86?

children.note: The returning officer collates station results openly and accurately and announces them promptly.
Systems to prevent cheating, including keeping election materials safe.

Parliament must create ways to settle election disputes quickly. A petition about any election except the presidential one must be filed within 28 days of the IEBC declaring the result, and may be served personally or by a notice in a national newspaper.
The deadline for petitions on MPs, senators, governors, county assembly members and women representatives.

manas.q: Within how many days must a non-presidential election petition be filed?

children.note: These follow Article 140 instead (Chapter 9), with their own shorter timetable.
Hand it to the respondent, or publish a notice in a newspaper read across Kenya.
The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission, constituencies and wards, and party-list seats.

This Article creates the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission, bars recent politicians and State officers from it, and makes it responsible for running or supervising all elections and referenda. Its eleven listed tasks run from voter registration to campaign-spending limits.

children.topic: Who may not be a member
children.note: Anyone who in the last five years was, or ran to be, an MP, county assembly member or party office-bearer, and anyone holding a State office. Members may not hold another public office.

manas.q: Who is barred from appointment to the IEBC under Article 88(2)?

children.note: The eleven jobs in clause 4, grouped.

manas.q: Name four tasks of the IEBC under Article 88(4).

children.note: Continuous registration and regular revision of the voters' roll; voter education.
Drawing constituencies and wards.
Regulating party nominations, registering candidates, the code of conduct, checking nomination rules are kept.
Limiting what candidates and parties may spend.
Settling disputes, including nomination disputes, but not election petitions after results are declared (courts do those).
Making observation, monitoring and evaluation of elections possible.
The IEBC is also one of the Chapter 15 independent commissions (Article 248).

Kenya has 290 constituencies, reviewed by the IEBC every 8 to 12 years and kept as close as possible to equal population. A review must finish at least a year before a general election, and anyone may ask the High Court to review a boundary decision within 30 days.
Each elects one member of the National Assembly (Article 97(1)(a)).

manas.q: How many constituencies does Article 89 fix?

children.note: Constituencies: every 8–12 years, done at least 12 months before a general election. Wards: reviewed periodically. New lines take effect when Parliament is next dissolved.
Kenya's population divided by how many constituencies (or wards) there are. Each unit aims for that number.

manas.q: What is the "population quota" in Article 89?

children.note: Up to 40% above or below the quota for cities and sparsely populated areas; up to 30% elsewhere, allowing for geography, community ties and communication.
If the quota were 160,000 people, a constituency in an ordinary area could hold between 112,000 and 208,000 (±30%); in a sparse area 96,000 to 224,000 (±40%).
Apply to the High Court within 30 days of the Gazette notice; the court must decide within three months.

Nominated and special seats in Parliament and county assemblies are filled by proportional representation from party lists. Parties share them in proportion to the seats they won, and the lists must alternate men and women and reflect Kenya's regional and ethnic diversity.
National Assembly 12 nominated (Article 97(1)(c)); Senate 16 women, 2 youth, 2 disability (Article 98(1)(b)–(d)); county assembly special seats (Article 177).
Lists alternate male and female in order of priority (except the Senate women's list, which is all women).

manas.q: What does Article 90 require about the order of men and women on a party list?

children.note: Except for county assemblies, each list must reflect regional and ethnic diversity.
In proportion to the seats each party's candidates won at the general election, not to votes cast.
What every party must and must not be, and the laws on parties.

children.topic: Art. 91 · What every political party must be
children.note: A party must be national in character, democratically run, and committed to unity, human rights, gender equality and the Constitution. It may not be built on religion, language, race, tribe, gender or region, use violence, keep a militia, bribe, or use public resources unless the law allows.

National character; elected leadership; regular free and fair internal elections; inclusion of minorities and marginalised groups; respect for rights and gender equality; obey the party code of conduct.

manas.q: Name three things every political party must do under Article 91(1).

children.note: Five prohibitions.

manas.q: Name three things a political party must not do under Article 91(2).

children.note: Not founded on religion, language, race, ethnicity, gender or region, and no hate advocacy.
No violence or intimidation against anyone.
No paramilitary or similar force.
No bribery or other corruption.
Except as this Chapter or an Act allows (for example the Political Parties Fund).
Parliament must legislate on fair broadcast airtime for parties, fair campaign broadcasting, and how parties are registered, run, funded, audited and kept from using public resources.
The Political Parties Act 2011 (Registrar of Political Parties, Political Parties Fund, Political Parties Disputes Tribunal). Check the current version on new.kenyalaw.org (checked 27 Nov 2026).

manas.q: Which Act carries out Article 92, and name one body it sets up.

children.note: Kenyan decisions read on Kenya Law (new.kenyalaw.org) that turned on this chapter. One line each; open the link for the judgment.

children.topic: Gender Representation Advisory Opinion, Supreme Court 2012
children.note: Asked about Article 81(b), the majority said the two-thirds gender rule for the National Assembly and Senate was to be achieved progressively, so it did not bind the March 2013 election, though it applied at once to county assemblies. Parliament was to pass the measures by 27 August 2015.

manas.q: What did the Supreme Court say in 2012 about when the two-thirds gender rule applies to Parliament?
